title: RhetorLint reviews visible wording, not people
claim: RhetorLint marks visible rhetorical patterns in supplied text and does not determine whether a claim is factually true.
scope: This statement describes the JavaScript reference engine and its published 0.1 output boundary as observed in the pinned source on 2026-08-03.
summary: The distinction matters when preparing public explanations: a wording prompt can help a reviewer notice pressure or hidden agency, but it cannot replace opening sources, checking facts, or obtaining publication authority.
why_now: A social release workflow needs a narrow review gate before it creates channel-specific drafts.
audience: People and agents preparing sourced public explanations

sources.title: RhetorLint README at the observed source commit
sources.locator: README.md, opening and ‘What it refuses to do’
sources.supports: The project says marks point to visible phrases and explicitly refuses person-reading and factual truth decisions.

sources.title: RhetorLint 0.1 output contract
sources.locator: spec/output.schema.json, mark.required and top-level result properties
sources.supports: The schema requires phrase text and exact offsets rather than a person-level verdict.

uncertainties: A deterministic rule pack deliberately under-marks and may also mark literal or harmless wording.
This record does not measure whether a reviewer will interpret a mark well.
call_to_action: Open the two pinned sources, then use the local explorer on wording you are responsible for reviewing.
